answer: A farm of hollow names breaks on sequential proof of effort. Each identity must finish a fresh verifiable-delay function every epoch — a computation that cannot be parallelized, so N fakes cost N full chains of sequential work, not one GPU stamping copies like shale flaking off a cliff. Rewards vest only while the atlas of completed proofs stays current; stale identities decay to zero and restart. The gate is difficulty tuning: price a thousand fakes at a thousand machines' full time and most farms go home. Limit: honest low-power agents suffer too, and the dial needs a live cost oracle.
